findings.title: Member profile editable by any authenticated user via member_id

evidence.why: ID source is Request.Form('member_id'), attacker controlled
No AND user_id = Session('UserID') check; relies on trust

findings.attack_scenario: User A sends POST /classic-asp/shop/member.asp?mode=edit with member_id=<User B's ID> and name='Hacked'. User B's profile is updated.
findings.impact: Modification of another user's personal data (name).
findings.recommendation: Add a check to verify the member_id belongs to the current session user before executing the update, or include AND user_id = Session('UserID') in the SQL query.

findings.title: Member profile deletable by any authenticated user via member_id

evidence.code: conn.Execute "DELETE FROM members WHERE member_id = " & Request.QueryString("member_id")
evidence.why: ID source is Request.QueryString('member_id'), attacker controlled; no ownership verification

findings.attack_scenario: User A sends GET /classic-asp/shop/member.asp?mode=delete&member_id=<User B's ID>. User B's account is deleted.
findings.recommendation: Add a check to verify the member_id belongs to the current session user before executing the delete, or include AND user_id = Session('UserID') in the SQL query.

findings.title: Order detail readable by any authenticated user via orderId

evidence.why: ID source is function argument passed from request
No user_id filter applied; relies on trust

findings.attack_scenario: User A sends GET /coldfusion/app/OrderService.cfc?method=getOrder&orderId=<User B's Order ID>. User A receives User B's order details.
findings.impact: Disclosure of another customer's order information (address, items).
findings.recommendation: Modify the query to include a condition filtering by the current user's ID (e.g., AND created_by = currentUserID).

findings.title: User deletable by any authenticated user via id

evidence.why: Endpoint accepts POST
ID source is parameter 'id' from request; no ownership check
Removes the found user without verifying if the current user owns it

findings.attack_scenario: User A sends POST /Admin/DeleteUser?id=<User B's ID>. User A deletes User B.
findings.recommendation: Verify that the user being deleted is owned by the current authenticated user (or ensure only Admins can access this endpoint and verify admin role).

findings.title: Password resettable by any authenticated user via id

evidence.why: Role check present
ID source is parameter 'id' from request; no ownership check against the specific user record

findings.attack_scenario: User A (who has Admin role) sends POST /Admin/ResetPassword?id=<User B's ID>. User A resets User B's password.
findings.impact: Account takeover of another user via password reset.
findings.recommendation: Verify that the user being reset is owned by the current authenticated user (or ensure only Admins can access this endpoint and verify admin role).

findings.title: User list exportable by any authenticated user via isAdmin flag

evidence.why: Endpoint accepts POST
ID source is parameter 'isAdmin' from request; no ownership check
Returns all users without filtering by current user

findings.attack_scenario: User A sends POST /Admin/Export?isAdmin=true. User A receives a list of all users in the system.
findings.impact: Disclosure of all user accounts (names, emails, etc.).
findings.recommendation: Verify that the user being exported is owned by the current authenticated user (or ensure only Admins can access this endpoint and verify admin role).

findings.title: Customer search results readable by any authenticated user via customer param

evidence.why: Endpoint accepts POST

evidence.code: var list = db.Database.SqlQuery<Invoice>("SELECT * FROM Invoices WHERE Customer = '" + customer + "'").ToList();
evidence.why: ID source is parameter 'customer' from request; no ownership check against current user

findings.attack_scenario: User A sends POST /Invoice/Search with customer=<Name of User B>. User A sees User B's invoices.
findings.impact: Disclosure of another user's invoice data.
findings.recommendation: Verify that the invoices returned belong to the current authenticated user.

findings.title: Order note editable by any authenticated user via OrderId

evidence.code: Dim sql As String = "UPDATE Orders SET Note = '" & txtNote.Text & "'"
evidence.why: ID source is hidden field hfOrderId.Value; attacker can manipulate it
No user_id filter applied; relies on trust

findings.attack_scenario: User A sends POST with hidden field hfOrderId=<User B's Order ID>. User A modifies User B's order note.
findings.impact: Modification of another user's order data.
findings.recommendation: Add a check to verify the OrderId belongs to the current session user before executing the update, or include AND UserId = Session('UserID') in the SQL query.

findings.title: Order detail readable by any authenticated user via order_no

evidence.code: ResultSet rs = c.createStatement().executeQuery("SELECT * FROM orders WHERE order_no = '" + no + "'");
evidence.why: No user_id filter applied; relies on trust

findings.attack_scenario: User A sends GET /order/detail.jsp?no=<User B's Order Number>. User A receives User B's order details.
findings.impact: Disclosure of another customer's order information (address, items).
findings.recommendation: Modify the query to include a condition filtering by the current user's ID (e.g., AND created_by = currentUserID).

findings.title: User email editable by any authenticated user via user_id param

evidence.why: ID source is parameter 'user_id' from request

evidence.code: PreparedStatement ps = conn.prepareStatement("UPDATE users SET email = '" + email + "' WHERE id = " + userId);
evidence.why: No user_id filter applied; relies on trust

findings.attack_scenario: User A sends POST /user/edit.do with user_id=<User B's ID> and email=hacked@example.com. User A modifies User B's email.
findings.impact: Modification of another user's personal data (email).
findings.recommendation: Add a check to verify the user_id belongs to the current session user before executing the update, or include AND id = currentUserID in the SQL query.
